props.name: stacked
props.description: Stacks the series on top of each other (default `false`)

props.name: percent
props.description: Scales the stacks to 100% (implies `stacked`; default `false`)

props.name: legend
props.description: Legend; shown by default when several series have a name

props.name: tooltip
props.description: Tooltip; `false` disables it

props.name: crosshair
props.description: Vertical guide line following the pointer

props.name: interaction
props.description: Zoom (Ctrl / ⌘ + wheel, pinch), pan (drag), double-click reset and keyboard navigation; `false` makes the chart static (default `true`)

props.name: area
props.description: Fills the area under the lines (default `false`)

props.name: labels
props.description: Overrides of the built-in texts of the `locale`

props.name: curve
props.description: Shape of the lines: straight, smooth (monotone) or steps

props.name: renderer
props.description: Backend of the data layer: `auto` tries WebGPU, then WebGL2, then WebGL, then Canvas2D (default `auto`)

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the chart; numbers are pixels (default `100%`)

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the chart (the legend included); numbers are pixels, strings any CSS length

props.name: series
props.description: Data series (replace the array or a `data` array to update the chart)

props.name: xAxis
props.description: X axis

props.name: yAxis
props.description: Y axis

props.name: annotations
props.description: Background areas and reference lines

props.name: padding
props.description: Space around the plot area, in pixels

props.name: palette
props.description: Series colors (defaults to the `--chart-series-1..8` CSS variables, then the theme colors)

props.name: ariaLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the chart

props.name: locale
props.description: BCP 47 locale of the texts and numbers the engine writes (tooltip, axes, accessible names); the page language by default

<script setup lang="ts">
// The labels follow the language of the closest ConfigProvider.
import { computed } from "vue";
import { useI18n } from "minerva-design/vue";
import { LineChart } from "minerva-design/vue/charts";

const TEXT = {
  en: {
    thisWeek: "This week",
    lastWeek: "Last week",
    days: ["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun"],
  },
  zh: {
    thisWeek: "本周",
    lastWeek: "上周",
    days: ["周一", "周二", "周三", "周四", "周五", "周六", "周日"],
  },
  ja: {
    thisWeek: "今週",
    lastWeek: "先週",
    days: ["月", "火", "水", "木", "金", "土", "日"],
  },
  fr: {
    thisWeek: "Cette semaine",
    lastWeek: "Semaine dernière",
    days: ["lun.", "mar.", "mer.", "jeu.", "ven.", "sam.", "dim."],
  },
};

const { language } = useI18n();
const text = computed(() => TEXT[language.value] ?? TEXT.en);
const series = computed(() => [
  { name: text.value.thisWeek, data: [820, 932, 901, 934, 1290, 1330, 1320] },
  { name: text.value.lastWeek, data: [620, 732, 701, 834, 1090, 1130, 1020] },
]);
</script>

<template>
  <LineChart
    :series="series"
    curve="smooth"
    :x-axis="{ type: 'category', categories: text.days }"
    :height="280"
  />
</template>

translationResources.title: Line chart
translationResources.description: Lines or filled areas over numbers, dates or categories. Handles millions of points on the GPU.

basic.title: Basic
basic.description: Two series over a category axis; the tooltip shows every series at the hovered x.

area.title: Area
area.description: area fills the space under the lines; the series opacity sets the fill.

curves.title: Curves
curves.description: curve sets the shape between the points: linear joins them with straight segments, smooth draws a monotone curve that never overshoots the data, step holds each value until the next point. A series can set its own curve.

stacked.title: Stacked
stacked.description: stacked piles the series so the top line is the total, and percent turns the stacks into shares of 100%. A y axis format replaces the percent ticks, so it is only set for amounts.

time-series.title: Time series
time-series.description: Date x values switch to a time axis; Intl.DateTimeFormat and Intl.NumberFormat write the dates and the compact y ticks in the reader's language.

large-data.title: 1,000,000 points
large-data.description: Typed-array columns with sorted timestamps: only the visible range is drawn. Ctrl / ⌘ + wheel to zoom.

traffic-events.title: Traffic with events
traffic-events.description: Daily visitors with a dashed x line for a product launch and a shaded area for an outage: annotations take the same timestamps as the data.

gaps.title: Missing data
gaps.description: A null y value leaves a gap instead of drawing a misleading line through the missing readings.

thresholds.title: Thresholds
thresholds.description: Server latency percentiles with a dashed y line for the objective and a red area above the critical level, so breaches stand out at a glance.

zoom.title: Range selector
zoom.description: Period buttons call setView on the chart ref with the visible window and a y range fitted to the prices inside it; Ctrl / ⌘ + wheel and drag still work.

live-sensor.title: Live sensor
live-sensor.description: A freezer probe streams one reading a second: setInterval appends a point and drops the oldest, so the time axis slides over the last minute, and the interval is cleared on pause and on unmount. A rect and a dashed y annotation mark the alarm zone; only the alarm state is announced.

log-scale.title: Logarithmic scale
log-scale.description: yAxis={{ type: "log" }} turns exponential growth into straight lines, so a lag of a few hours and populations from 10³ to 10⁹ stay readable together; the switch compares it with the linear scale. Intl.NumberFormat with notation: "scientific" writes the ticks.

measure.title: Measure between two points
measure.description: onPointClick pins up to two days and the readout gives the change between them; x line annotations and a green or red rect mark the period, and onPlotClick on an empty area clears the measurement.

index-tooltip.title: Indexed performance
index-tooltip.description: Four asset classes rebased to 100 at the start; renderTooltip replaces the default content with a React list sorted from the best to the worst performer, with the color of each series and its change since the base.

small-multiples.title: Small multiples
small-multiples.description: One small LineChart per city in a CSS grid, all with the same yAxis min and max so the panels compare at a glance; interaction={false} keeps them static and a dashed y line marks the WHO guideline.

props.height: Height of the chart, the legend included: pixels or any CSS length
props.options: Other engine options (axes, legend, tooltip, palette, format…) merged with the element's own properties; property only
props.instance: The engine instance (minerva-design/charts/core), null until the element is rendered and connected

events.minerva-hover: The hovered (or keyboard-focused) points changed; detail: { x, xLabel, items }, null when nothing is hovered
events.minerva-point-click: A point or a bar was clicked; detail: { x, xLabel, items }
events.minerva-plot-click: The plot area was clicked where there is no point; detail: { x, y } in data coordinates
events.minerva-zoom: The user zoomed or panned; detail: { x, y } (the visible ranges)
events.minerva-renderer-change: The backend is ready, or fell back after a GPU loss; detail: { renderer }

methods.getView: Visible range, null before the engine is created
methods.getRenderer: Backend in use (webgpu, webgl2, webgl, canvas2d), null until ready
